title: The projects I turned down last year, and why
excerpt: A small studio is shaped as much by the work it refuses as by the work it shows. Seven enquiries I declined, and what each one taught me.
content:
A small studio is shaped as much by the work it refuses as by the work it shows. Last year I said no to seven enquiries. None of them was a bad client. Each was a bad fit, which is harder to spot and more expensive to ignore.

When the deadline is the brief

Three of the seven needed an identity in under three weeks. It can be done, and the result always looks like it. I now ask one question first: what happens if this launches a month later? If the honest answer is "nothing much", there is time to do it properly.

When nobody can decide

Two had no single person who could approve the work. A committee can choose between options, but it cannot commission a point of view. I offered a short workshop to agree who decides, and one of them took it.

A good no is specific. It says what would have to change for the answer to be yes.

If you are weighing up a project and are not sure it is ready for a designer, write to me anyway. Sometimes the useful answer is "not yet".
